hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $\overline{BD}$

Under this transformation, each point on the circle maps to another point which is also on the circle.


[[☃ image 1]]

The circle is *symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A circle with a center labeled A. A point B is directly across from point D on the circle. A point C is directly across from point E on the circle. A blue line connects from points D to point B, reflecting the circle across it. The image of the circle fits on the pre-image.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $\overline{CD}$

Under this transformation, some points on the circle map to another point which is no longer on the circle.  


[[☃ image 1]]

The circle is *not symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A circle with a center labeled A. A point B is directly across from point D on the circle. A point C is directly across from point E on the circle. A blue line connects from points D to point C, reflecting the circle across it. The image of the circle does not fit on the pre-image.

hints.content:
The symmetries that apply to the circle are:

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{BD}$ | Yes
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{CD}$ | No
